analysis.title: UBS US Equity Weekly
key_insights: Politics has overtaken macro as the immediate market driver after the Democratic midterm sweep. The debate shifts toward policy risk around AI and data centres. AI investment has contributed roughly 1ppt to recent GDP growth, and cumulative AI buildout plans are estimated at $10.3tn through 2032.
The key question on data-centre policy is whether policymakers stop development or require hyperscalers to fund their own power, grid connections and water infrastructure.

UBS Economics still sees the Fed biased toward 25bp hikes in December and January unless labour markets deteriorate materially. Around 50% of PCE components are running above 3%, and AI investment offsets some of the growth risk.
2027 AI visibility remains strong: cloud growth is expected to accelerate from 64% in 2026 to 97% in 2027, cloud backlog is ~3.5x forward 12-month sales and US data-centre vacancy is below 2%.
Beyond 2027 the funding question gets harder. Top-13 hyperscaler capex is forecast at $1.77tn vs $1.47tn of operating cash flow, a ~$300bn funding gap.
Palantir (Buy, PT $250) grew revenue 96% and US Commercial 148%, validating enterprise AI adoption despite flat RPO.

Tighter data-centre regulation could raise electrical and cooling content per MW, because self-sufficient capacity needs more power generation, conversion and redundancy, and higher rack densities and water limits increase cooling equipment. After a 35%+ de-rating, AI Industrials trade around 16x 2028E EPS vs 20x+ through-cycle. Johnson Controls (Buy, PT $190) is the preferred exposure, with Eaton, nVent, Vertiv, INNIO and Modine also preferred.

Thursday's sell-off changed market internals: 85% of S&P 500 constituents declined, SPX fell 4.7%, NDX 6.4% and SOXX 12.2%, and VIX jumped almost 12 points toward 29. The 3x-long SOXL fund fell 39% and is ~75% below early-October levels.

Fundamentals look healthier than the tape. Q3 SPX EPS is running +31.6%, the referenced 8,100 year-end target implies >10% upside, and lower oil and yields with stabilising rate-sensitive assets fit a correction inside an uptrend more than a recession.

Amgen (Buy, PT $530 from $470) reported $10.4bn revenue vs $10.1bn consensus and EPS of $6.45 vs $5.79. Repatha grew 37%, Evenity 39% and Imdelltra 128%. MariTide Phase III obesity data around Feb/Mar 2027 is the major catalyst.
Vertex (Buy, PT $640 from $615) has a Povetacicept decision on 30 November, followed by early-2027 Inaxaplin data with an estimated 65-70% probability of success and potential 10-20% share upside.

Protagonist Therapeutics (Buy, PT $184): Mimrylo royalties are forecast at $55m in 2027 vs $28m consensus. UBS is also more constructive on delayed AVANZAR/Dato-DXd data, and Merck's Sac-TMT could become a $10bn+ franchise.

US nominal retail growth could slow toward ~3.5% annually through 2045, which favours share gainers Walmart (Buy, PT $130) and Costco (Buy, PT $1,275). Ageing shifts spending toward healthcare, food and home maintenance.
Dutch Bros (Buy, PT $75): Q3 system comps reached 4.4%, traffic stayed positive and ~250 shops are planned for 2027 vs ~215 consensus.
Starbucks (Neutral, PT $110 from $105): turnaround is more credible, with ~4% comps and 13.5-14.0% FY27 margins achievable, but ~33x FY27E EPS already discounts significant recovery.

Tactical 1-3 month Softlines preference on a geopolitical (Iran-conflict) resolution via lower fuel and freight costs and recovering Middle East demand: Gap (Buy, $42), Under Armour (Buy, $8), PVH (Buy, $121), Carter's (Neutral, $33), G-III (Neutral, $27). Underlying ratings are unchanged.

Rivian upgraded to Buy from Neutral (PT $17): R2 demo drives exceeded 103k in Q3 vs >57k in Q2, UBS assumes ~82k R2 deliveries in 2027, automotive gross margin could turn positive in Q1'27 and approach 9% by Q4. Liquidity is ~$7.1bn, potentially ~$13bn with targeted capital.
StandardAero (Buy, PT $34 from $32): 2027 capacity is essentially sold out, Q3 EBITDA grew 15%, margins expanded 130bp to 14.4%, and a $350m accelerated repurchase adds support.

Auto aftermarket preferences are AutoZone (Buy, PT $4,230) and O'Reilly (Buy, PT $122), supported by an ageing US vehicle parc. AutoZone's mega hubs can cut delivery times from ~3 hours to as little as 45 minutes.

3M (Buy, PT $230) settled ~99% of current PFAS personal-injury claims at a $5.8bn present-value cost vs ~$10bn investor expectations, alongside a $6bn buyback authorisation. UBS forecasts 2027 EPS of $10.47 vs $9.92 consensus.

Packaging Corp. of America (Buy, PT $289): effective containerboard supply looks tighter than headline capacity, Greif synergies are $40-50m annualised vs a $60m target, and UBS expects ~30% EPS growth in 2027. The DOJ investigation is the key overhang.

Demographics: the global silver economy could reach ~$8tn annually by 2030. US population growth slowed from 1.3% in 1993 to 0.5% in 2025, and 74% of the projected 9.1m increase in households over the next decade is headed by someone 65+.
Viatris (Buy, PT $28 from $26) has improving 2027 EBITDA and potential EXPAREL IP-related re-rating. Amneal (Buy, PT $28 from $25) is the cleaner earnings-growth story.

GRAIL (Buy, PT $175) is the preferred post-earnings diagnostics setup. Galleri volumes missed, but the Q1'27 FDA decision and later CMS reimbursement matter more, and repeat patients rose to ~36% from ~30%. Veracyte faces a growth reset, and Caris looks closer to fair value.
Kontoor Brands (Buy, PT $125 from $136) has a path to $7+ FY27 EPS, Q3 gross margin up 240bp and ~$450m of planned repurchases, yet trades ~12x FY27E earnings vs ~19% expected five-year EPS CAGR.

FICO (Neutral, PT $942): Q4 beat, but FY27 guidance was withheld as mortgage pricing shifts to bespoke contracts and VantageScore adds competition. FY27 EPS falls to $45.50 from $51.25 and buybacks are paused.

Positioning: hedge funds and asset managers entered the midterms significantly bearish USD, then equity weakness and stronger payrolls triggered a safe-haven USD rally. China Tech became a relative winner on policy support and short-covering of the crowded long-memory/short-China trade.
